about: The epistola of the formulary “Saint Luke the Evangelist” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Brethren: I give thanks to God, who has put the same earnest care for you into the heart of Titus; for he indeed accepted the appeal, but being more earnest, he set out to you of his own will. We have also sent with him the brother whose praise is in the Gospel throughout all the churches; and not only that, but he was also appointed by the churches as the companion of our journey in this grace, which is administered by us for the glory of the Lord and for our resolved will: avoiding this, lest anyone should find fault with us in this abundance which is administered by us. For we take thought for what is good, not only before God, but also before men. And we have sent with them our brother as well, whom we have often proved in many things to be earnest, but now much more earnest, with great confidence in you, whether for Titus, who is my companion and helper toward you, or our brethren, the apostles of the churches, the glory of Christ. Show them, therefore, before the face of the churches, the proof of your love and of our glory on your behalf.
